clue.text: It may end with a landing, indoors or out

definitions.text: It may end with a landing, indoors or out

parts.words: It may end with a landing, indoors or out
parts.note: indoors, a run of stairs finishes at a landing; outdoors, an aeroplane journey finishes when the plane touches down

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses share the same word: a set of stairs inside a house and a journey by air outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A staircase run ending at a landing and an air journey ending with touchdown share one name.

clue.text: See a student in urban neighbourhood

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: in places the small pieces inside the town word

parts.note: urban means of a city
L is a learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: Someone is told to visit a student who lives in a town district.
explanation.walkthrough: LO is an archaic exclamation meaning 'look!', and L for learner comes from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A district or area is the sense shared with neighbourhood.

clue.text: Such good tidings — lame dog's cured

indicators.note: a cured animal is put right, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Happy news: an injured dog has recovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cured' rearranges LAMEDOGS; the possessive apostrophe gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Good tidings are joyful, cheerful news, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Forbearing to show Leo tipsy in unconscious state

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged name inside the state of unconsciousness

parts.note: a trance is a dazed or unconscious state

indicators.note: a tipsy person staggers about, so the letters of Leo are shuffled

explanation.surface: A drunk Leo, out cold, shows patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipsy' gives OLE, the anagram of Leo; 'in' places it inside the unconscious state. 'Forbearing' is read as a noun here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbearing, as a noun, means patient endurance, the same sense as this word.

clue.text: Material for building many on the island

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
taken as written
Crete is the large Greek island

explanation.surface: Someone describes the stone or timber used for building on a crowded island.
explanation.definitionFit: This mix of cement, sand and gravel is a standard construction substance.

clue.text: Waits for these, one of them written by Dickens

definitions.text: Waits for these, one of them written by Dickens

parts.words: Waits for these, one of them written by Dickens
parts.note: waits are street singers who go round at Christmas; they sing seasonal songs, and Dickens wrote a famous story with that title in the singular

explanation.walkthrough: 'Waits' looks like a verb; it is a noun for bands of carol singers, and Dickens's novella 'A Christmas Carol' is the one written by him.
explanation.definitionFit: Waits sing seasonal songs at the door, and Dickens wrote a story named after one.

clue.text: Happy with what's inside?

explanation.definitionFit: The word means satisfied and also, stressed differently, the material held within something.

clue.text: Chopper lifted explosive device over point he aims to pass…

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means raised up, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an axe is a chopping tool
a mine is a buried explosive
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A helicopter carries a bomb over a spot, leading into a person who wants to get through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns AXE upward to EXA; 'over' just places it above the rest in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate sitting a test hopes to pass it.

clue.text: …he'll not forget the size of the paper

definitions.meaning: the saying goes that this animal never forgets
a large traditional paper size, about 28 by 23 inches

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 7 down, but the clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says this beast never forgets, and it is also the name of a large paper format.

clue.text: Opening of story, slow mover, one with characters ill-defined

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so take the start of story

parts.note: a crawler is something that moves slowly, like a caterpillar

explanation.surface: A list of things: the start of a tale, a sluggish creature, and someone whose personality is vague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' suggests people in a story, but here it means handwritten letters, which this person forms badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes untidily forms letters that are hard to make out.

clue.text: Where Frenchmen enjoy a swim? Sounds crazy

indicators.note: signals that the phrase before it is said aloud to give a word spelt differently

parts.note: Parisians might bathe in the Seine, the river through Paris, so they swim in Seine

explanation.surface: A question about where French people go swimming, answered with a remark that it seems mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad and unhinged are synonyms of this word.

clue.text: Every variety appealing to suckers

definitions.meaning: all kinds, every type there is
Liquorice ... are a British mixed sweet, attractive to those who suck sweets

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means all kinds, and Liquorice Allsorts are a popular British assortment of sweets meant for sucking.

clue.text: Made of iron, this strange object of desire

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: something strange is out of its usual order, so the letters of this are rearranged

explanation.surface: A peculiar thing made of iron that someone longs for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges the four letters of 'this' to follow iron's symbol; 'Made of' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixation is an object of obsessive desire, often an inanimate thing.

clue.text: Twelfth Night session of patience here

definitions.text: Twelfth Night session of patience here

parts.words: Twelfth Night session of patience here
parts.note: in Shakespeare's play Viola describes a lovesick girl who 'sat like Patience on a', a statue's plinth, so this is where Patience sat

explanation.walkthrough: 'session' and 'patience' suggest a card game; the reference is the line in Twelfth Night about Patience sitting on a memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare pictures Patience as a statue sitting on a memorial, so it is where Patience held her session.

clue.text: Maybe one King of Frogs, it's possible he'll find new words

indicators.note: maybe says the letters of one may be ordered differently

parts.note: in Aesop's fable the frogs asked Jupiter for a king and were given King Log

indicators.note: possible says the letters of it's could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Perhaps one ruler of frogs is able to discover new vocabulary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' and 'possible' each rearrange the short word beside them. King Log is from Aesop: the frogs asked for a king and were sent a log.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who coins or uses newly made terms invents new vocabulary.

clue.text: Neat house made by a soldier

parts.note: taken as written
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army's sappers, so a soldier

explanation.surface: A tidy home built by a man in the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like 'tidy', but it is an old word for cattle, so a neat house is a cowshed.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an old word for cattle, and this is a cowshed where they are housed.

clue.text: Party with French beard and pigtail, say

parts.note: barbe is French for beard

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a queue is a plait of hair hanging at the back

explanation.surface: A party attended by someone with a French beard and a pigtail.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor party where food is grilled over charcoal.

clue.text: Freckles scraped off from this foolhardy

indicators.note: from this tells the solver to take the letters out of the run of clue words just before it

explanation.surface: Scraping freckles off one's face is a rash thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'Freckles scraped', running from the second letter of the first word to the first of the second; 'off' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash and heedless of danger are synonyms.

clue.text: A break may help the making of one

definitions.text: A break may help the making of one

parts.words: A break may help the making of one
parts.note: a pause is another word for it, and in snooker a cue support helps a player make a break of points

explanation.walkthrough: In snooker a break is a run of scoring shots, and the cue support of this name helps a player make one; a break is also a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: It means a pause, and it is also the stick a snooker player uses to support the cue.

clue.text: Faithful old keeper

parts.note: a long-serving household servant, and also a device that holds something in place, such as a dental brace

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a loyal old family servant; a dental brace that holds teeth in place is also a keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-serving family servant, and also a device that holds something in place.

clue.text: Foolish shrew heard in the compound

indicators.note: heard means the phrase is spoken, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: silly Kate: Katherine is the shrew in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew

explanation.surface: A stupid nagging woman is overheard in the enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a walled enclosure but is a chemical compound; 'shrew' is Shakespeare's Kate.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt of silicic acid is a chemical compound found in many rocks.

clue.text: Sounding of a note -chief element of comedy

definitions.meaning: the pitch heard from a musical key
the central stone of an arch is the chief element

explanation.walkthrough: Split, the answer reads as a key's tone; whole, it is the central stone of an arch and the name of the silent comedy studio.
explanation.definitionFit: A key's pitch heard aloud; also the central wedge holding an arch, and Mack Sennett's slapstick film studio.

clue.text: Relative makes royal valet lose his gravity

indicators.note: lose means a letter is taken away from the phrase

parts.note: a servant of the monarch is a king's man
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A family member makes the king's servant lose his solemn manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gravity' looks like seriousness but is G.
explanation.definitionFit: A male family member is a blood relation.

clue.text: Graduated ruler for kitchen work

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is what a graduate holds
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A monarch who has a degree is put to work in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooking in an oven, such as making bread, is a task done in the kitchen.

clue.text: Like mint initially found in Croatia perhaps

indicators.note: one piece is found inside another, so the letter goes into the rearranged country
perhaps signals that the word Croatia may be arranged differently
initially means the first letter of mint

explanation.surface: Asking whether something like mint is grown in Croatia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CROATIA, and 'found in' places M, the first letter of mint, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint is a fragrant herb, and fragrant is the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Like something vanishing from a lady's boudoir

definitions.text: Like something vanishing from a lady's boudoir

parts.words: Like something vanishing from a lady's boudoir
parts.note: vanishing cream is a cosmetic kept on a dressing table, so the adjective describing it is smooth and rich

explanation.walkthrough: 'vanishing' suggests something disappearing, but vanishing cream is a skin cosmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanishing cream is a cosmetic, so something resembling it is rich and smooth in texture.

clue.text: "Tea, although an --, Is a gentleman at least" (Chester-ton)

definitions.text: "Tea, although an --, Is a gentleman at least" (Chester-ton)

parts.words: "Tea, although an --, Is a gentleman at least" (Chester-ton)
parts.note: G K Chesterton's poem The Song of Right and Wrong calls tea an Eastern thing yet a gentleman, unlike cocoa; fill the gap

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-gap quotation from G K Chesterton: tea comes from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea comes from Asia, so Chesterton calls it an Eastern native.

clue.text: An angular ratio's between two points — no difficulty here

indicators.note: between puts the middle part inside the pair of compass letters

parts.note: E and S are two points of the compass
taken as written
the sine is a trigonometric ratio of an angle

explanation.surface: A trigonometry problem set between two places, with no difficulty involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of difficulty is a synonym for the ease this word names.

clue.text: Country's Yuletide fare

definitions.meaning: the nation spanning Europe and Asia whose capital is Ankara
the bird traditionally roasted for Christmas dinner

explanation.definitionFit: It is the nation with capital Ankara and also the roast bird eaten at Christmas.
